parole.significato: Chicane (obstruction designed to reduce speed), double road bend
parole.testo: From chicaner, ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *skikkijan. Related to French chic.

parole.significato: to stroke gently, to touch lightly
parole.testo: From Middle French effleurer, from Old French esflourer, equivalent to ex- (“ex-”) + fleurer (“sprinkle”). In some senses, from Middle French fleur (“surface, top layer”), ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *flōr (“ground, floor”), from Proto-Germanic *flōraz.

parole.significato: thick fog that tends to freeze
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle French frimas, from Old French frimas, an extended form of Old French frime (“hoarfrost”), from Proto-West Germanic *hrīm (“hoarfrost”), from Proto-Germanic *hrīmô (“hoarfrost”), related to Old English hrīm (“hoarfrost”). More at rime.

From Old French grosele (13th c.), from a Proto-West Germanic *krōsilā, possibly related with *krūs (“curly, frizzy”). Cognate with Walloon gurzale. For Germanic cognates see Luxembourgish Kréischel. Compare also Dutch kruisbes.

parole.significato: owl (specifically, those species of owls with ear tufts; those without ear tufts are chouettes)
parole.testo: Ultimately imitative. Possibly from or influenced by a descendant of Proto-West Germanic *hūō. Compare Old High German hūwo, ūvo, (h)ūwila and, as a borrowing into Romance, Catalan òbila, òliba. If so, related to English owl. Compare also Latin būbō.
